question: The Green Revolution in India primarily focused on improving the production of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**wheat and rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s and it primarily focused on improving the agricultural production of major food grains, especially wheat and rice.
 
• This revolution led to the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, particularly for wheat and rice, which significantly boosted the production and yield per hectare.
 
• The initiative was largely funded and supported by various international organizations, including the Rockefeller Foundation and the Ford Foundation.
 
• Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is considered as the father of the Green Revolution in India for his pivotal role in the development and introduction of these high-yielding variety seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that occurred between the 1940s and the late 1960s, which increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries.
 
• It involved the development and dissemination of new seed varieties, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and the implementation of new agricultural practices such as irrigation and mechanization.
 
• The primary goal was to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains and to combat hunger and malnutrition.
 
• Despite its success in increasing food production, the Green Revolution also led to environmental and social issues, such as soil degradation, water scarcity, and increased inequality among farmers.
 
 
 
• **High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:**
 
 
• HYV seeds are a type of seed that has been bred to produce more yield per acre than traditional varieties.
 
• These seeds are often resistant to certain diseases and pests, and they respond well to fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• The use of HYV seeds was a key component of the Green Revolution, significantly increasing the production of staple crops like wheat and rice.
 
• However, HYV seeds often require more inputs (such as water and fertilizers) and can lead to monoculture practices, which may reduce biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan:**
 
 
• Dr. Monkombu Sambasivan Swaminathan is an Indian geneticist and international administrator, renowned for his leading role in India's Green Revolution.
 
• He is known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for his work in the development of high-yielding variety seeds.
 
• Dr. Swaminathan's efforts led to significant increases in food grain production in India, helping to alleviate hunger and improve food security in the country.
 
• He has received numerous awards and honors for his contributions to agriculture and food security, including the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Vibhushan.
